title: Watch your cashflow
caption: A million euros is coming, and the company is gone.
late: The million lands one month late

costs-begin-before-customers.description: Company setup and the founders' living costs arise before a startup has users or income.[1]

startup-funding.title: Paul Graham, A Student's Guide to Startups: Startup Funding

high-burn-rate-is-a-clock.header: A high burn rate is a clock
high-burn-rate-is-a-clock.description: It puts a startup under constant time pressure, and the stated remedy is to spend little while working fast.[1]

startup-funding.title: Paul Graham, A Student's Guide to Startups: Startup Funding

default-alive-test.description: Ask whether the company reaches profitability on its remaining money at current expenses and growth; worrying too early is cheap, worrying too late is dangerous.[1]

default-alive.title: Paul Graham, Default Alive or Default Dead?

walk-the-months.title: Walk the months
walk-the-months.script: Read it with me. January, you start with 100 thousand in cash and 50 thousand goes out. February, another 50 thousand goes out, and at the end of February your cash is zero.

march-has-no-money.title: March has no money
march-has-no-money.script: March arrives and the cost lands on an empty account, with nothing to pay it. The big number sits in April, one month late.

antithesis.title: Antithesis
antithesis.script: A million euros is coming, and the company is gone. Right on paper, dead on the calendar.

hand-over-the-verdict.title: Hand over the verdict
hand-over-the-verdict.script: So find your own February: the month your cash hits zero. And if that is the month you run out, when would you have needed to start selling?
